item.title: Critical React, Check Point, N-central and Windchill RCE Threats Dominate
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Nov 11:00 → 12 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

PHP2Shell Exploitation on Check Point Gateway — Must Read

Attackers exploited unpatched Check Point Mobile Access gateways using PHP2Shell and CVE-2026-123039, deploying PhiliKit-linked TSGA/TSProxy backdoors and, in some Israeli intrusions, pivoting to ESXi hosts to run the destroy_v6 wiper. The campaign has links to China-nexus UNC5221 tooling, but its destructive, Israel-focused elements leave attribution uncertain.

  • Beginning on October 30, 2026, attackers targeted unpatched Check Point Security Gateways through Mobile Access portals using activity consistent with PHP2Shell exploitation.
  • After initial access, the attackers exploited CVE-2026-123039 in the DynamicCLI interface to gain root-level control and installed PHP webshells plus the TSGA and TSProxy backdoors.
  • The attackers used the gogo scanner to identify internal systems, accessed a VMware ESXi host over SSH using the vpxuser account, and executed the destroy_v6 wiper in the destructive stage.
  • The first wave focused on Israeli organizations and included destructive activity in some cases, while a November 2 wave targeted organizations in multiple countries without observed destructive activity.
  • TSGA and TSProxy share code, configuration, and cryptographic material with the PhiliKit framework, but the article states that the operation’s true nature and attribution cannot be assessed with high confidence.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, remote-access, hypervisor

Products: check-point-security-gateways, mobile-access, vmware-esxi

Vendors: check-point, vmware

CVE-2026-126187: React Server Components Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Code Through Smuggled Flight Rows — Must Read

React Server Components packages before 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1 reportedly contain a critical Flight transport framing flaw that can enable unauthenticated server-side code execution under specific shared-ArrayBuffer conditions. Upgrade affected React/framework dependencies, rebuild and redeploy, and avoid sending multiple typed-array views over a shared ArrayBuffer until patched.

  • CVE-2026-126187 is described as a critical, unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in React Server Components, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.5.
  • The affected packages are react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack in versions through 19.0.8, 19.1.9, 19.2.8, and 19.3.0.
  • The issue requires a response containing multiple typed-array views over a shared ArrayBuffer, attacker-influenced bytes in one view, and a downstream path that transfers the backing storage.
  • React fixed the issue in versions 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1 by copying large typed-array payloads into exact-size buffers before sending them.
  • Organizations should upgrade framework-managed or direct dependencies, confirm the resolved package versions in lockfiles, and rebuild and redeploy affected applications.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: react-server-components, react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, react-server-dom-turbopack, next-js, secure-registry, oss-package-search, dev-machine-guard

Vendors: react, stepsecurity, vercel

New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access — Should Read

New public exploits dubbed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell reportedly bypass N-able’s recent N-central patch, enabling unauthenticated root RCE on exposed servers and SYSTEM-level command execution on managed Windows agents. N-able says the server issue requires the non-default Legacy API to be enabled and internet-accessible, and urges customers to disable it immediately.

  • N-able is investigating a public disclosure alleging additional vulnerabilities in on-premise N-central version 2026.4.1 HF2.
  • N-able said the server issue depends on the Legacy API being enabled and exposed to the public internet, although the feature is disabled by default and not recommended.
  • Researcher Sean Bales said the 4EverAble2Shell proof of concept can enable unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges on N-central servers patched to build 2026.4.1.26.
  • Bales said Agent2Shell combines more than 10 zero-day vulnerabilities to run commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on managed Windows agents when an attacker knows the target appliance ID.
  • Previdian and watchTowr reported observing probes targeting 4EverAble2Shell, but Previdian said there was no evidence of successful exploitation at the time of writing.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: n-central, apache-axis

Vendors: n-able, apache-software-foundation

PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution — Should Read

PTC released patches for CVE-2026-126325, a critical 9.2-severity deserialization flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM that could let remote attackers execute code. Organizations running self-hosted affected versions should patch immediately or restrict network exposure, especially given prior active exploitation of Windchill flaws by Cl0p-linked actors.

  • PTC released patches for CVE-2026-126325, a critical remote code execution flaw affecting Windchill and FlexPLM with a CVSS v4 score of 9.2.
  • The flaw involves improper input validation and deserialization of untrusted data, allowing remote code execution through crafted requests.
  • PTC said customers whose Windchill or FlexPLM environments are hosted by PTC have already had the patches applied.
  • Organizations operating non-PTC-hosted affected systems are urged to patch promptly or apply network restrictions if patching cannot happen immediately.
  • A prior critical Windchill and FlexPLM flaw, CVE-2026-12569, was actively exploited and later used by Cl0p-linked actors to deploy JSP web shells and steal sensitive product data.

Products: windchill, flexplm

Vendors: ptc

Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments — Should Read

Kazakhstan-linked espionage group Silent Lynx used a DeepSeek-powered Hermes AI agent, controlled through Telegram, to automate reconnaissance, data theft and cleanup during intrusions into Central Asian government networks. The group reportedly accessed Tajikistan’s railway and government document systems and also compromised an Uzbek forestry platform.

  • CloudSEK found an exposed server associated with Silent Lynx containing more than a dozen gigabytes of stolen government documents, hacking tools, and records of AI-agent use.
  • The operator used the open-source Hermes AI agent, primarily with DeepSeek models, for reconnaissance, data collection, and removing traces from compromised systems.
  • Silent Lynx maintained access to Tajikistan’s national railway network from at least mid-August through early October and stole databases with login credentials, internal documents, and operational reports.
  • Using a railway employee’s credentials, the group accessed Tajikistan’s national electronic document management platform and automated downloads of thousands of documents, including documents sent to or processed by the Defense Ministry in 2026.
  • CloudSEK found evidence of a compromise involving Uzbekistan’s Smart Forestry server and malicious files posing as Turkmenistan official documents that appeared to be prepared for a phishing campaign.

Products: hermes, telegram

Vendors: cloudsek, deepseek

Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign — Should Read

Material Security uncovered a phishing campaign that used trusted Google Calendar and Drive links plus Nyasher reverse proxies to steal live Google Workspace sessions while bypassing conventional link reputation and MFA protections. The campaign relied on compromised sender accounts and rapidly rotating infrastructure, prompting hundreds of Cloudflare-backed takedowns.

  • Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has used Google Calendar invites and later Google Drive sharing invitations to target corporate Google users.
  • The campaign used Google redirect links, compromised sender accounts, and a live reverse proxy called Nyasher to capture active Google sessions after victims completed real sign-in and multi-factor authentication prompts.
  • Material Security reported malicious gateways and endpoints to Cloudflare, which placed phishing warnings in front of confirmed fake interstitials and proxied Google sign-in pages.
  • During one month of Operation CloudFire, researchers recorded 68,676 blocked campaign messages, 2,112 unique malicious URLs, 897 unique domains taken down, and 8,570 compromised sender addresses across 6,354 root domains.
  • A stolen live Google session can provide access to email, Google Drive, and the ability to grant OAuth access in the victim's name.

Technologies: identity-provider, mfa, proxy, email-security, cloud-platform

Products: google-workspace, google-calendar, google-drive, cloudflare-turnstile, microsoft-365, nyasher

Vendors: google, cloudflare, material-security, microsoft, intuit

Romania says it stopped Russian cyberattack targeting government emails — Should Read

Romania’s intelligence service says it contained a December 2025 cyberespionage intrusion attributed to Russia-linked Turla that targeted government Microsoft Exchange email servers, including communications with NATO and EU institutions. Officials said no sensitive data exfiltration was identified.

  • Romania’s intelligence service said it detected and contained a December 2025 intrusion targeting an unspecified government institution and restored the affected email service.
  • The Romanian Intelligence Service attributed the operation to Turla, a Russian cyberespionage group linked to Russia’s Federal Security Service.
  • ESET said Turla used previously unknown malware called Cereal to compromise government Microsoft Exchange email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan.
  • According to ESET, the malware in Romania was configured to intercept emails sent to or received from NATO and European Union institutions.
  • Romania said it found no evidence that sensitive data was taken and shared information about the incident with relevant authorities and European intelligence partners.

Technologies: email-security

Products: microsoft-exchange-server, cereal

Vendors: microsoft, eset

Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues — Should Read

Microsoft says Windows updates released since October 2026 Patch Tuesday can cause SQL Server linked-server queries using OLE DB to leave external database connections open, degrading performance and stability. An out-of-band fix is expected within days; administrators can contact Microsoft Support for an interim mitigation.

  • Microsoft confirmed that Windows updates released since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday can cause SQL Server performance and stability issues.
  • The issue affects SQL Server linked-server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases, including known Oracle and PostgreSQL connections.
  • Affected queries can leave connections open after completion, causing the number of open external database connections to grow and degrading server performance over time.
  • The problem affects Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2012 and later, and Microsoft plans to release an out-of-band Windows update within days.
  • Administrators can manually close leftover connections or restart the SQL service as a temporary measure, but these actions can terminate active queries and the issue may return.

Technologies: operating-system, database

Products: windows-10, windows-11, windows-server-2012, windows-server-2025, sql-server

Vendors: microsoft, oracle, postgresql

Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs — Should Read

Google Cloud warns that three AMD EPYC Turin transient scheduler side-channel flaws could expose data between processes inside a VM; customers must apply guest OS patches and stop then start affected VMs once Google’s CPU-information update is available. Google has already mitigated cross-VM and VM-to-host risks, while bare-metal users need firmware and OS updates.

  • Google Cloud warned that three AMD EPYC Turin CPU flaws could allow code running on the same processor core inside a virtual machine to infer data from other processes or the kernel.
  • Google says it has already applied mitigations for attacks between virtual machines and between virtual machines and the host, while affected machine series include C4D, N4D, H4D, Z4D, and G4.
  • The flaws are TSA-SQ (CVE-2024-36350), TSA-L1 (CVE-2024-36357), and the newly disclosed CVE-2026-0004, also called TSA-Fill by the Xen Project.
  • Affected Google Cloud VM customers should install their operating system vendor’s fix when available and stop then start the VM after Google’s CPU-information update arrives, because a guest reboot alone is insufficient.
  • AMD says full mitigation for Turin servers on customer-owned hardware requires both platform firmware and operating-system updates, and may affect performance.

Technologies: cloud-platform, hypervisor, container-platform, operating-system

Products: google-compute-engine, amd-epyc-turin, xen-hypervisor, google-kubernetes-engine, cloud-run, linux-kernel

Vendors: google-cloud, amd, xen-project, debian

Hijacked email accounts complicate investigations into European bomb hoaxes — Should Read

Mass bomb-hoax emails targeting schools, airports and newsrooms across Europe were sent through compromised accounts at legitimate institutions, helping them bypass email checks and complicating attribution. Authorities deem the threats non-credible, but cross-border investigations are challenged by anonymized access and slow international evidence requests.

  • Bomb-hoax emails sent to thousands of schools across Europe were transmitted through a compromised Da-Yeh University email account in Taiwan.
  • Authorities in Scotland and Ireland assessed the school threats as not credible, while the messages nonetheless prompted evacuations in Italy.
  • Proofpoint said the threats it examined came from compromised accounts rather than forged sender addresses, helping the emails pass authentication checks and avoid spam filters.
  • Investigators face obstacles because account-access records may be obscured by VPNs or proxy networks and evidence must be sought across multiple jurisdictions.
  • No government has attributed the hoaxes to a specific actor, although some messages were signed by "fighters of the Male State" or "Mikhail Andropov."

Vendors: proofpoint

FDA Flags Cyber, AI Risks in Autonomous Medical Robots — Optional

FDA and cybersecurity experts warn that autonomous and remotely operated medical robots can expose patients to real-time harm if attackers hijack communications, inject commands, or disrupt device performance. They recommend cyber-informed clinical risk assessments linking technical threats to patient-safety outcomes.

  • Federal regulators and cybersecurity experts warn that cyberattacks, AI malfunctions, and communications failures in robotic medical devices could cause serious patient harm before clinicians can intervene.
  • Phil Englert of Health-ISAC said remotely operated and autonomous medical devices add risk because the communication link between operator and device becomes part of the potential exposure.
  • Potential actions against these devices include taking over sessions, sending commands, stealing credentials, causing service disruption, and introducing packet loss or delay that affects device performance.
  • Health-ISAC recommends cyber-informed clinical risk assessments that evaluate how each cybersecurity threat could affect clinical care or patient safety.
  • According to Englert, a cyberattack on a robotic medical device could influence clinical decisions or alter patient treatment in real time.

Top AI network and infrastructure pentesting tools in 2026 — Optional

The article compares six AI-driven network and infrastructure pentesting tools, recommending Aikido Security for external attack-surface testing and Pentera or Horizon3 NodeZero for internal network and Active Directory testing. It emphasizes choosing tools based on attacker starting point, deployment requirements, AI autonomy, and whether remediation retests can identify newly introduced exposure.

  • The article distinguishes external network infrastructure pentesting, which examines internet-facing systems, from internal network infrastructure pentesting, which examines internal systems and Active Directory from an assumed foothold.
  • Aikido Security is presented as an external network pentesting option that begins with verified domains, discovers internet-facing assets, and includes retesting intended to identify whether fixes created new entry points.
  • Pentera and Horizon3 NodeZero are presented as options for internal network and Active Directory testing, with internal testing requiring a system deployed inside the organization’s network.
  • The article states that annual pentest reports can become outdated as organizations make frequent production changes, leaving newly deployed hosts untested until a later engagement.
  • The article advises buyers to assess where an attacker would start, what decisions the tool’s AI makes, what must be installed, and whether remediation verification checks more than the original finding.

Technologies: identity-provider, cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, source-control

Products: aikido-security, pentera, nodezero, ridgebot, hadrian, escape, active-directory, kubernetes, azure

Vendors: aikido-security, pentera, horizon3, ridge-security, hadrian, escape, microsoft

Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them — Optional

A forthcoming webinar will discuss how integrating real-time identity context with SIEM and EDR alerts can help SOC teams assess permissions, blast radius, and safe containment options for human, machine, and AI identities.

  • The article promotes a free webinar titled “Fuel the SOC with Identity Context: Securing Humans, Machines, and AI Agents.”
  • Security operations teams may detect suspicious activity but lack information about the identity involved, its permissions, and the systems it can access.
  • Service accounts, API keys, automated workloads, and AI agents can access important systems and data, increasing the complexity of security investigations.
  • Connecting identity information with existing SIEM and EDR alerts can help analysts assess potential lateral movement and respond without unnecessarily disrupting critical automation.
  • The webinar will cover practical methods for enriching alerts with identity context, investigating lateral movement, assessing potential attack impact, and aligning IAM and security operations workflows.

Technologies: siem, edr, iam

item.title: WFX GitHub Secrets Campaign, GSocket Persistence, and Critical MongoDB and Node.js Flaws
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Nov 07:00 → 12 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

WFX Phantom: The GitHub Actions Secret Stealer That Deletes Its Tracks — Must Read

WFX Phantom is a large-scale GitHub Actions secret-stealing campaign that uses stolen developer and bot tokens to inject a CI payload, steal secrets and cloud credentials, then quickly revert commits and delete workflow runs. Organizations should immediately hunt for its PR and commit indicators, treat affected workflow-accessible credentials as compromised, and remove AWS/Azure persistence mechanisms.

  • Beginning November 10, 2026, attackers used stolen GitHub tokens to add the WFX secret stealer to repositories where those tokens had write access, then typically reverted the commit and deleted the associated GitHub Actions run within a minute.
  • The campaign used probe pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from branches named "wfx-docs"; GitHub search showed more than 63,000 such pull requests as of November 12, although only some repositories received the payload.
  • WFX collects GitHub Actions secrets, runner-process memory, cloud credentials, repository data, and recent workflow artifacts, and it can attempt persistence through AWS role-policy changes, IAM access keys, and Azure federated identity credentials.
  • The payload was hidden in modified workflows, existing shell scripts, new audit workflow files, or hidden .ci-*.sh scripts executed through npm hooks, allowing it to run even when a workflow file was not visibly changed.
  • Later samples sent stolen data exclusively to a Telegram chat through api.telegram.org, so blocking the campaign's previously observed collection IP addresses alone no longer stopped the newest versions.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, iam, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, package-registry

Products: github-actions, fly-io-github-app, harden-runner, github-audit-log, malicious-files-for-github, aws-iam, azure-active-directory, microsoft-graph, azure-key-vault, google-cloud-platform, hashicorp-vault, npm

Vendors: github, fly-io, stepsecurity, amazon-web-services, microsoft, google, telegram, hashicorp

Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover — Must Read

MongoDB has patched CVE-2026-118383, a critical pre-authentication use-after-free flaw that can crash a replica-set member if it later becomes primary while behind on replication. Organizations should upgrade all self-managed replica-set members promptly and restrict database network access until patched.

  • MongoDB has released fixed versions for CVE-2026-118383, a critical use-after-free flaw rated 9.5 out of 10 that can be triggered by two unauthenticated requests.
  • The flaw affects MongoDB replica-set members, including shard and configuration server members in sharded clusters, but does not affect standalone mongod servers.
  • A targeted member crashes only if it later wins an election to become primary while it is behind on recent changes, causing cleanup during catch-up to reuse memory that has already been freed.
  • Datadog Security Labs reproduced the issue in a lab and found that enabling authentication on vulnerable versions did not block the two requests.
  • MongoDB Atlas clusters receive fixed versions automatically during maintenance, while self-managed deployments must upgrade every replica-set member and should restrict database network access until they can patch.

Technologies: database, cloud-platform

Products: mongodb-server, mongodb-atlas

Vendors: mongodb, datadog

Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data — Must Read

Node.js released security updates for supported 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines that fix 16 flaws, including critical HTTP/2 and HTTPS issues that can crash servers, leak cross-connection memory, and potentially expose TLS private keys. Organizations running Node.js servers should upgrade to 22.23.5, 24.22.3, or 26.13.1 immediately, as no workarounds are listed and end-of-life versions remain unpatched.

  • Node.js released versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1 to fix 16 vulnerabilities, seven of which are rated high severity.
  • CVE-2026-123863 can let an unauthenticated client crash default Node.js HTTP/2 servers on the 24.x and 26.x lines when the server responds before a request body has fully arrived.
  • CVE-2026-123866 can cause affected Node.js HTTP/2 servers to send a client memory contents that may include responses intended for other connections.
  • CVE-2026-123864 affects Node.js HTTPS servers and may allow an unauthenticated client to read memory from other connections, including TLS private keys and other users’ requests, under specified handler conditions.
  • Node.js lists updating as the only fix, provides no workaround for servers that cannot update, and says end-of-life lines including 20.x and 25.x remain affected.

Products: node-js

Vendors: node-js, anthropic

Attackers turn NIKKE’s game launcher into malware — Should Read

Attackers abused NIKKE’s legitimate server-pushed launcher task channel to deliver a Lua-based infostealer disguised as a log file, allowing credential, crypto-wallet, and developer-secret theft from within the signed launcher process. Players who used the launcher during the attack window should treat their systems as compromised and rotate affected credentials and wallet seeds.

  • Attackers abused NIKKE’s legitimate server-pushed task channel to make its launcher download a malicious LuaJIT payload disguised as a normal log file.
  • The payload, called k2f-agent by Bitdefender, ran inside the signed launcher process and included 46 modules for credential theft, file collection, remote commands, and cleanup.
  • The stealer targeted saved passwords and cookies from Chrome, Edge, and Opera, five cryptocurrency wallet browser extensions, and potentially developer and system secrets such as SSH keys, GPG keys, Git credentials, and Kubernetes configurations.
  • Stolen information was sent through the launcher’s existing encrypted telemetry channel, while download, data collection, exfiltration, and cleanup occurred in less than ten minutes.
  • Bitdefender stated that its Advanced Threat Defense stopped the launcher on observed protected systems before personal information could be exfiltrated, and the Iceland-hosted malicious delivery server was later taken down.

Technologies: browser, antivirus, operating-system

Products: goddess-of-victory-nikke, nikke-launcher, bitdefender-advanced-threat-defense, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, opera, metamask, phantom, coinbase-wallet, keplr, tronlink, luajit, chromium-embedded-framework

Vendors: bitdefender, shift-up, level-infinite, google, microsoft, opera, metamask, phantom, coinbase, keplr, tronlink, luajit-project, chromium-embedded-framework-project

Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access — Should Read

Threat actors are increasingly abusing the legitimate GSocket remote-access tool to persist on compromised Linux web and hosting servers through outbound, encrypted relay connections that evade inbound firewall controls. Administrators should remove GSocket artifacts, audit persistence mechanisms, restrict outbound traffic, and patch exposed systems.

  • Multiple threat actors are abusing the open-source GSocket remote-access tool to retain access to Linux servers after the initial entry vulnerabilities have been patched.
  • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint telemetry recorded a 356.2% increase in GSocket-related detections between March and August.
  • GSocket routes encrypted sessions through the Global Socket Relay Network using outbound connections from both the compromised host and the attacker, so the host does not need an inbound listener or public IP address.
  • Of detected GSocket incidents, 87.1% involved web applications and hosting environments, with PHP web applications and cPanel hosting accounting for 63.9% and Apache accounting for 24.3%.
  • Microsoft recommends removing GSocket-related files, confirming relay-network connections have stopped, restricting outbound traffic, and auditing cron jobs, systemd services, and shell startup files for unauthorized additions.

Technologies: remote-access, edr, operating-system, web-server

Products: gsocket, microsoft-defender-for-endpoint, cpanel, apache-http-server, linux-kernel

Vendors: microsoft, hackers-choice, cpanel, apache-software-foundation, linux-kernel-project

Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues — Should Read

Microsoft says a limited number of Windows 11 devices that installed the October 2026 preview update may fail to install November’s KB5132061 security update, showing errors including 0x800f0989 and 0x800f0993. The company says an automatic repair should resolve the issue within 24–48 hours without user action.

  • Microsoft confirmed that some Windows 11 devices are unable to complete installation of the November 2026 security update KB5132061.
  • The issue affects a limited number of devices that installed the October 2026 non-security preview update KB5127936; devices that did not install that preview update are not affected.
  • Affected devices may repeatedly attempt the update or display error codes 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993.
  • Microsoft said it would automatically repair affected devices within 24 to 48 hours beginning November 11, 2026, after which the November security update should download and install through Windows Update.
  • Microsoft advised IT administrators to contact Microsoft Support if reports of installation problems continue after 48 hours.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-11, windows-update

Vendors: microsoft

Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works — Optional

Effective cloud pentesting focuses on proving whether attackers can cross trust boundaries between tenant workloads, provider-managed services, control planes, and underlying infrastructure—not merely finding code execution or open ports. Tests should safely verify real cross-tenant or provider-level impact through minimal, authorized actions.

  • Cloud penetration testing should assess whether attackers can cross trust boundaries between tenant resources, provider-managed services, internal provider components, and underlying infrastructure rather than merely identify open ports or achieve code execution.
  • The article models cloud platforms in three layers: the public External layer, the provider’s logical Overlay layer for service runtimes and internal components, and the physical and virtualization-focused Underlay layer.
  • A confirmed trust-boundary violation requires more than seeing or authenticating to an internal service; the tester must obtain authorization and safely perform a controlled action outside the original boundary.
  • Service account credentials, network access, and runtime context must be evaluated together because an over-privileged credential can enable access to internal APIs even when network segmentation is strict.
  • Cloud pentests of provider infrastructure require separate authorization and should confirm cross-tenant effects only with controlled test tenants and synthetic data.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, hypervisor, database, iam, object-storage, message-queue, ci-cd, source-control, backup

Products: azure-cosmos-db, azure-container-instances, gitlab, kubernetes, openstack, ceph, rabbitmq, open-vswitch, saltstack, libvirt, postgresql

Vendors: microsoft, gitlab, openinfra-foundation, kubernetes-project, ceph-project, rabbitmq, salt-project, postgresql-global-development-group

item.title: Apache CVE-2026-119618 and ScreenConnect Rogue Client Attacks Lead Digest
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Nov 03:00 → 12 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely — Must Read

Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55–2.4.70 has a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618) when HTTP/2 is enabled; upgrade to 2.4.71 or disable h2/h2c until patched.

  • CVE-2026-119618 is a critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled.
  • The flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71.
  • Red Hat released fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10, while Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier are not affected.
  • Debian unstable has been fixed with apache2 2.4.71-1, while Debian bookworm, trixie, and forky were listed as vulnerable and Amazon Linux releases were awaiting fixes.
  • Organizations unable to update can remove h2 and h2c from Apache's Protocols directive and leave Protocols http/1.1 as a temporary mitigation.

Technologies: web-server, operating-system

Products: apache-http-server, mod-http2, mod-h2, red-hat-enterprise-linux, amazon-linux, debian

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, red-hat, debian, amazon-web-services, anthropic, google-cloud, icing

ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients — Must Read

Attackers are abusing compromised ConnectWise ScreenConnect panels or operator sessions to deploy rogue clients and the SCKit toolkit, affecting at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions as a precaution, while investigators have found no evidence of a ScreenConnect vulnerability or compromise of ConnectWise infrastructure.

  • ConnectWise disabled five third-party ScreenConnect extensions as a precaution after reports of unauthorized access, while stating it found no evidence of a ScreenConnect vulnerability or compromise of its own infrastructure.
  • Huntress observed attackers use cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients to at least 288 managed endpoints across 48 organizations.
  • The observed activity uses the SCKit toolkit to establish persistent remote access, create a relay mechanism for intercepting session cookies, add Microsoft Defender exclusions, and create a scheduled task named TrapWatch.
  • Huntress said available telemetry points to compromised credentials or hijacked operator sessions as possible initial access methods, although the exact method remains unclear.
  • Sophos observed unauthorized ScreenConnect client deployments from three ScreenConnect instance IDs, including commands that downloaded and silently installed a ScreenConnect client from an identified IP address.

Technologies: remote-access, antivirus

Products: screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Vendors: connectwise, huntress, sophos, microsoft

Can Agentic AI Investigate a Phishing Campaign? Evidence Walkthrough — Optional

Agentic AI can accelerate phishing investigations by gathering evidence across domains, cloned pages, search results, and infrastructure, but humans must validate attribution and approve any external or production actions. Because attackers can embed prompt-injection instructions in phishing content, agents need evidence trails, strict permissions, and controls that treat fetched content as untrusted data.

  • Agentic AI can independently collect phishing-investigation evidence such as domain registration details, safely captured web pages, related infrastructure, and indicators, but the article recommends human approval for actions such as blocks and takedown requests.
  • A Microsoft randomized trial involving 167 security analysts found that analysts using the Security Copilot Phishing Triage Agent found up to 6.5 times more true positives per minute and were up to 77% more accurate, although the article notes the trial used Microsoft's own product and test corpus.
  • The article uses lookalike Microsoft Teams domains, including teams-online[.]com, teams-livemeeting[.]com, and teams-cloud[.]live, to show how an investigation can connect cloned pages, young privacy-protected registrations, search placement, and a fake update lure.
  • The article warns that attackers can place hidden instructions in phishing emails, attachments, and web content intended to influence AI systems that read or summarize them.
  • It recommends treating all fetched content as untrusted data, separating read access from action permissions, requiring evidence for each verdict claim, logging tool calls, and retaining human approval for actions outside the organization.

Technologies: email-security, soar

Products: security-copilot-phishing-triage-agent, microsoft-defender, microsoft-teams, blaze-ai

Compromised GitHub accounts push CI secret stealer to tens of thousands of repositories — Must Read

A threat actor used thousands of compromised GitHub accounts to inject short-lived malicious CI workflows into tens of thousands of repositories, stealing GitHub Actions secrets, cloud credentials, and other runner data. Organizations should immediately investigate the listed branches, pull requests, commits, and workflow indicators and rotate any credentials accessible to affected workflows.

  • Beginning November 10, a threat actor used stolen GitHub credentials to open probe pull requests in 61,764 repositories and then inject malicious payloads designed to steal CI secrets and cloud credentials.
  • The article identified evidence that the payload ran in at least 1,806 repositories, while the attacker deleted workflow runs and logs after collecting credentials.
  • Affected repositories may contain a wfx-docs branch, a pull request titled "docs: dependency audit notes," or commits such as "ci: refresh build cache" and "chore: add ci helper."
  • The payload can collect GitHub Actions secrets and variables, workflow tokens, cloud credentials, runner environment data, repository contents, caches, and build artifacts.
  • The campaign reached Packagist package digitalelvis/neuronai-studio version 3.14.3 and GitHub Go module github.com/onuragtas/docker-env versions v1.0.278 and v1.0.280.

ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know — Should Read

Unit 42 reports that attackers are using AI-powered red-team frameworks such as ARTEX to autonomously probe exposed identity flows and APIs, rapidly validate credentials, and pursue cloud access at scale. Defenders should reduce public attack surface, protect self-service and write endpoints, remove exposed specifications and secrets, and detect the distinctive high-volume, adaptive behavior of autonomous agents.

  • Unit 42 observed ARTEX in intrusion attempts against multiple targets and investigated intrusions where attacker infrastructure hosted an ARTEX console or used ARTEX-associated infrastructure and user agents.
  • As of October 2026, Unit 42 identified 1,323 internet-facing hosts running CyberStrikeAI and 609 running ARTEX, including 21 hosts running both tools.
  • The article states that ARTEX can adapt after failed attempts, target internet-exposed identity workflows and APIs, and use associated credentials and trust relationships to reach cloud environments.
  • Observed ARTEX-like activity included brief request bursts followed by 25–31 second pauses, rapid validation of more than 200 client secrets, immediate targeting of routes found in OpenAPI specifications and source maps, and successful retries after HTTP 422 errors.
  • Unit 42 recommends removing public OpenAPI specifications, source maps and configuration files containing tokens or client IDs; requiring authentication for every write endpoint; hardening password-reset and registration flows; and hunting for behavior such as canary usernames, new-IP cloud-key use, and write-then-delete storage tests.

Baker Tilly disclosed that a breach at an unnamed third-party service provider exposed client and dependent data, including names, addresses, and Social Security numbers. More than 10,000 Texans were affected, and the firm is offering 24 months of Experian credit and identity monitoring.

Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations — Must Read

Attackers are compromising MSP ScreenConnect environments to push rogue remote-access clients to customer devices, affecting at least six MSPs and 286 endpoints across 47 organizations. ConnectWise and Huntress urge partners to avoid interactive sessions with suspected compromised devices, review Run Command history, revoke sessions, reset credentials, and check for listed indicators of compromise.

  • Huntress identified an active campaign in which compromised cloud-hosted ScreenConnect environments at managed service providers were used to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients to customer devices.
  • As of Huntress’s report, the campaign had affected six managed service providers and at least 286 endpoints across 47 organizations, with the number continuing to rise.
  • The attackers used ScreenConnect’s Run Command feature to install remote-access clients outside the legitimate managed service provider’s ScreenConnect environment.
  • ConnectWise said it was investigating the malicious activity and advised partners to avoid interactive sessions with suspected compromised devices, review account activity, revoke active sessions, reset credentials from a trusted device, and verify multifactor authentication.

eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates after private key mishap — Should Read

eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate CA certificates after a faulty key-transfer script exposed RSA private-key material in host memory, bringing the total affected intermediates to 16. The incident prompted major vendors to block the compromised trust chains, and eMudhra plans to exit the publicly trusted TLS certificate business.

  • eMudhra revoked eight additional RSA intermediate certificate authority certificates after finding that a custom Python key-transfer script processed private-key material in the host computer's memory rather than solely inside secure hardware.
  • The additional revocations bring the total number of affected eMudhra intermediate certificates to 16, including eight ECDSA certificates whose private keys were reduced to one byte and could be recovered by testing 256 values.
  • The flawed script was used in April 2025 to transfer certificate authority keys between hardware security module vendors after delays obtaining new hardware.
  • Mozilla, Google, Apple, and Microsoft released protections to block trust in the compromised eMudhra certificate chains.
  • eMudhra plans to leave the publicly trusted TLS certificate business, stop issuing under its remaining G1 hierarchy by November 16, and has commissioned a KPMG review expected by December 4.

Notion says a breach at AI vendor Fireworks AI exposed Notion AI chat transcripts from its Insights dataset for less than 1% of users. Affected users should review incident notices and rotate any passwords, API keys, or credentials entered in those chats.

Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation — Must Read

Zoom patched two critical Zoom Workplace for Windows flaws, CVE-2026-108186 and CVE-2026-108187, that could let unauthenticated remote attackers escalate privileges. Organizations should update to version 7.1.8 or later to remediate the affected versions.

  • Zoom released updates for Zoom Workplace for Windows to address two security flaws that could enable privilege escalation.
  • CVE-2026-108186 is an improper input validation flaw with a CVSS score of 9.6 that affects Zoom Workplace for Windows versions 7.1.0 through before 7.1.8.
  • CVE-2026-108187 is an origin validation flaw with a CVSS score of 8.1 that affects Zoom Workplace for Windows versions before 7.1.5.
  • According to the article, either flaw could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to escalate privileges without special permissions or access.
  • Zoom did not state that these vulnerabilities are being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to apply the latest patches.

The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar — Should Read

Unit 42 uncovered Falcon (XG), a browser-based espionage framework used against government targets in the Middle East and Southeast Asia to steal credentials, emails, cookies and communications through injected JavaScript and malicious Chrome/Firefox extensions. Falcon can also deploy the Rust-based Antino implant, which uses Microsoft OneDrive for command and control and persistence.

  • Unit 42 identified Falcon, also called XG or Xiàng Gē, as a command-and-control framework that uses malicious JavaScript in compromised websites to control and collect data from victims’ browsers.
  • Falcon was observed targeting government entities in one Middle Eastern country and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, including foreign affairs, defense, interior, law-enforcement and justice organizations.
  • Falcon can sideload Chrome and Firefox extensions disguised as a PDF viewer, giving operators access to browser credentials, cookies, web traffic, clipboard activity, browsing history, downloads and selected messaging services.
  • Falcon maintains encrypted WebSocket communications and can use a victim’s browser as a proxy to access resources with that victim’s saved credentials and active login sessions.
  • Falcon also delivered Antino, a Rust-based Windows implant that uses Microsoft OneDrive to receive commands, upload data and establish persistence through the Windows Registry Run key.

Iran-backed network directed London attacks over FaceTime, US prosecutors say — Should Read

U.S. prosecutors allege that an IRGC-linked Kataib Hezbollah network remotely directed and recorded arson, stabbing, and attempted attacks on Jewish, American, and military-linked sites across Europe, including London, using FaceTime and other apps. Evidence recovered from a defendant’s seized iPhone reportedly documented the coordination, propaganda recordings, and plots including an attempted attack on RAF Fairford.

  • A U.S. superseding indictment alleges that three men linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kataib Hezbollah orchestrated attacks and attempted attacks at Jewish, American, and military-linked sites across Europe.
  • Prosecutors say attackers in London received live instructions over FaceTime during arson incidents targeting a Jewish charity building, Iran International, and a synagogue, while the calls were recorded for propaganda.
  • The indictment alleges that the network later planned an attack on RAF Fairford using vans, fuel, potential shrapnel, and intended explosives, but British authorities reported finding petrol and no explosives after stopping the vehicles.
  • Much of the cited evidence was recovered from Mohammad al-Saadi’s iPhone, including recorded FaceTime calls, raw attack footage, and messages with a Kataib Hezbollah contact.

Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million — Should Read

Maersk confirmed a breach of an isolated legacy LF Logistics system, while the WhiteArmor ransomware group claims it stole about 100GB of data and is demanding $5 million. Maersk says there is no evidence that sensitive data or other company and customer systems were affected.

Attackers are hosting the AntiFox open-source AI penetration-testing platform on Alibaba Cloud to automate intrusions against web servers and AWS environments, including webshell deployment and theft of production secrets. Defenders should investigate unusual IIS activity alongside bursts of denied and successful AWS API calls, then revoke exposed credentials and sessions.

A Potential Binance Employee’s Mac Was Infected Seconds After a Fake Homebrew Ad — Should Read

An anonymized infostealer log suggests a potential Binance employee’s Mac was compromised by MacSync just 16 seconds after clicking a Google ad leading to a fake Homebrew page in March 2026. The stolen data included a Mac password, Okta-related credentials, and access to internal data-platform tools, but the report finds no evidence linking this specific infection to Binance’s later theft.

eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice — Optional

eBPF’s legitimate kernel capabilities are increasingly being adapted into stealthy Linux rootkits that can hide processes, filter traffic, and activate on crafted network packets without loading traditional kernel modules. Defenders should tightly restrict eBPF privileges, inventory loaded programs and XDP attachments, and monitor for suspicious BPF activity and packet triggers.

  • Flare reported that Russian-language underground forum posts shared eBPF rootkit code and instructions for hiding processes and activating implants with specially crafted network packets.
  • eBPF programs can operate through Linux’s legitimate bpf() interface without loading a traditional kernel module, so routine lsmod checks may not detect them.
  • Prior Linux malware and research projects, including BPFDoor, Symbiote, ebpfkit, TripleCross, Boopkit, and LinkPro, have demonstrated BPF or eBPF techniques for stealth, traffic handling, or remote activation.
  • Flare found that one tutorial described hooking getdents64 to hide processes, using XDP to inspect incoming HTTP traffic, and encrypting command-and-control traffic with AES-256-GCM.
  • The article recommends that Linux operators audit loaded eBPF programs, restrict eBPF privileges, patch BPF verifier flaws, and watch for unexpected XDP programs and suspicious packet triggers.

item.title: Qlik Sense Attacks, Windows DHCP CVE-2026-88243, and CRAFTY FALCON API Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 11 Nov 11:00 → 11 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

CERT-In’s CRAFTY FALCON Advisory: AI Is the Accelerant, Your Payment APIs Are the Target — Must Read

CERT-In warns that the active CRAFTY FALCON campaign is using AI-assisted offensive tools to exploit weak staging environments, shared credentials, and trusted payment API paths to steal funds from Indian financial organizations. Defenses should prioritize strict production isolation, short-lived secrets, server-side payment validation, cloud monitoring, and rapid fraud detection.

  • CERT-In says the active CRAFTY FALCON campaign targets Indian NBFCs, digital lenders, fintechs, payment firms, and cryptocurrency exchanges by abusing their payment and disbursement APIs.
  • The campaign gains access through exposed UAT or staging servers, hardcoded API tokens, plaintext credentials, missing MFA, and flaws in file-upload or deserialization functionality.
  • Attackers move from non-production to production environments through shared credentials and network paths, then use legitimate AWS Systems Manager and Lambda channels to run commands.
  • CERT-In reports that attackers test routes with Rs 1 transfers before sending larger amounts to mule accounts, including through merchant settlement APIs.
  • The advisory recommends separating non-production from production, replacing IP-based trust with server-side signed requests and mutual TLS or scoped keys, rotating long-lived secrets, and monitoring cloud-control-plane activity.

Technologies: cloud-platform, remote-access, container-platform, source-control

Products: artex, pentagi, cairn, cyberstrikeai, aws-systems-manager, aws-lambda, github

Vendors: amazon-web-services, docker, github

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-88243) Windows DHCP Server Remote Code Execution via Out-of-Bounds Read — Must Read

Microsoft’s November 2026 updates patch CVE-2026-88243, a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in the Windows DHCP Server service affecting Windows Server 2016 through 2025. Organizations should urgently patch DHCP servers and block untrusted inbound UDP/67 exposure.

  • CVE-2026-88243 is a critical out-of-bounds read flaw in the Windows DHCP Server service that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code remotely over a network.
  • Microsoft addressed the vulnerability in its November 2026 security updates, with affected Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025 builds requiring the relevant fixes.
  • The vulnerability has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 and requires no credentials, privileges, user interaction, or high attack complexity.
  • At the time of writing, the issue was not listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and no public proof of concept had been reported.
  • Organizations should inventory servers with the DHCP Server role, block inbound UDP/67 from untrusted networks, audit cloud security groups, and monitor DHCP Server logs for crashes or unexpected restarts.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-server, windows-dhcp-server, cycognito-platform

Vendors: microsoft, cycognito

Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits — Should Read

Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers in Europe with PowerShell reverse shells and infrastructure containing ActiveMQ and Veeam exploit tooling, echoing tactics associated with past CACTUS ransomware intrusions. Organizations should patch Qlik Sense and monitor for scheduler.exe-launched PowerShell, OpenSSH persistence, and connections to 45.115.26.23.

  • Cynet detected attempts in October 2026 to run PowerShell reverse-shell commands on Qlik Sense servers belonging to several European Union-based customers within a period of just over three minutes.
  • The attempted reverse shell connected to 45.115.26[.]23 on port 4455 and was executed under scheduler.exe, but the attempts were blocked.
  • The exact Qlik Sense vulnerability used in the latest activity is unknown, although the activity overlaps with a November 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign that exploited Qlik Sense flaws.
  • Analysis of the attackers’ infrastructure found a Windows Go backdoor, SSH persistence scripts, an Apache ActiveMQ exploit for CVE-2023-46604, and a modified Veeam toolchain for CVE-2024-40711.
  • A PowerShell script variant attempted to install OpenSSH and create a scheduled task named WinUpdCheck to run a reverse shell every five minutes.

Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords — Should Read

Researchers found that 35,578 of 37,571 publicly discoverable Grok-built apps were accessible without sign-in, exposing internal and personal data from dozens of organizations, including xAI and X. The issue is amplified by insecure default sharing settings, DNS discoverability, and test apps with flawed access controls.

  • Claroc found 35,578 of 37,571 Grok-built apps online were accessible without sign-in, and estimated that about 2% of the open apps contained high- or critical-severity material.
  • The exposed apps included 24 created by X and SpaceXSI staff, with examples such as a confidential sales-hire onboarding plan, a 594-account sales territory map, and a confidential X advertising proposal to a U.S. federal agency.
  • Researchers identified internal data from 30 additional organizations, including a hospital employee directory, an intensive-care patient briefing, a fire department shift board, and a contractor timesheet application containing employee passwords in plain text.
  • Claroc said Grok publishes apps on grok.me subdomains and defaults the sharing setting to “Anyone with the link,” while passive DNS records can reveal those subdomains.
  • In tests on their own Grok apps, the researchers found that one app had no sign-in protection and another allowed an uninvited account to access, edit, and delete customer data because its membership check was implemented incorrectly.

Vendors: xai, claroc, openai

eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise — Should Read

eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate certificate authorities after discovering that their RSA private keys were exported into a Python process during a flawed 2025 key-transfer ceremony, despite initially saying they were unaffected. The incident expands the company’s certificate-authority failures and reinforces its planned exit from the publicly trusted TLS business.

  • eMudhra revoked eight additional intermediate certificate authorities after determining that their RSA private keys had been read from hardware security modules into a Python process during an April 30, 2025 key-transfer practice run.
  • The company had previously said the eight RSA issuers were unaffected, but later concluded it could not demonstrate that their key material had been handled in accordance with its own rules.
  • Six of the newly revoked authorities issued website certificates and two issued code-signing certificates; eMudhra listed 195 certificates from them and said all holders had been moved to new certificates.
  • The same script had reduced eight separate ECDSA private keys to a single leading byte, leading to the October compromise and revocation of those authorities.
  • eMudhra says it knows of no misuse, while Microsoft, Chrome, Firefox, and Apple are ending or limiting trust in certificates from its remaining G1 hierarchy on the stated schedules.

Poland temporarily took its ePUAP government services platform offline after detecting and stopping a cyberattack, though officials say no compromise or data theft has been confirmed. The outage also affects ePUAP mailboxes and may disrupt the Trusted Profile digital identity service until security checks are complete.

  • Poland temporarily shut down the ePUAP government services platform after detecting and stopping a cyberattack.
  • ePUAP enables citizens and businesses to submit official documents, communicate with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online.
  • Officials said ePUAP was taken offline as a precaution and have not confirmed that government systems were accessed or that sensitive information was stolen.
  • ePUAP electronic mailboxes remain unavailable, and the disruption may temporarily affect the Trusted Profile digital identity system.

Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms — Should Read

Britain, France, and 12 other governments endorsed voluntary guidelines for commercial spyware and hacking firms, calling for customer vetting, safeguards against misuse, and suspension of sales where abuse is likely. The non-binding rules create no penalties and rely on government buyers and export controls for enforcement.

  • Fourteen governments in the Britain- and France-led Pall Mall Process adopted voluntary guidelines for businesses that develop, sell, or finance commercial cyber intrusion capabilities.
  • The guidelines call on companies to vet customers, implement safeguards against misuse, monitor and report abuses, and halt sales and support when serious misuse presents a credible risk.
  • The guidelines are non-binding, impose no penalties for non-compliance, and are expected to rely on governments that buy the tools and license their export for enforcement pressure.
  • The tools covered can silently penetrate phones and have been used for intelligence and organized-crime investigations but have also been implicated in surveillance of journalists, political officials, activists, and businesses.
  • The guidelines were endorsed at the Pall Mall Process’s third conference, attended by representatives from 43 countries, with signatories including the United Kingdom, France, the United States, Germany, Italy, and Japan.

We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned. — Optional

Browser-based AI agents often operate inside a user’s authenticated session, making their actions indistinguishable from the user’s and potentially giving them excessive, untraceable access. Until standards support agent identity, verifiable human delegation, and task-scoped permissions, organizations should discover, constrain, audit, and require step-up approval for sensitive agent-driven actions.

  • Token’s Rehearsal browser agent operates within a user’s authenticated session, so the application server cannot inherently distinguish its actions from those of the user.
  • Because Token controls both Rehearsal and its platform, it can lock the interface while the agent acts, record all agent moves, and limit the agent to read-only dashboard access unless the user approves a change.
  • The article says Chrome and Microsoft provide some controls for agentic browsing, while WebMCP can expose website actions to agents and Web Bot Auth can verify which agent made a request.
  • The article argues that current approaches do not combine agent identity, proof of the person an agent represents, and a permission scope narrower than that person’s access.
  • It recommends that security teams inventory agents that use authenticated sessions, trace their users and access, identify agent-based paths around access controls, and require explicit approval or stronger sign-in checks for sensitive actions.
